title: Office Associate
subtitle: A placeholder week at a mid-size company in Pune

days.title: Monday: first day at your desk
days.realTalk: PLACEHOLDER: replace with a real quote from a working professional, e.g. "Nobody tells you how much of the job is just keeping track of things."

scenes.text: You log in and find 23 unread emails. Your manager, Meera, wants a status update by noon. Where do you start?

choices.text: Sort every email into folders first, then start working
choices.outcome: Took 40 minutes, but now you know exactly what's on your plate.

choices.text: Reply to the urgent-looking ones and skip the rest
choices.outcome: You cleared the fires. A few small things might slip through.

choices.text: Walk over and ask Meera what matters most today
choices.outcome: Meera looks pleased. "Just the vendor report. Ignore the rest for now."

scenes.text: Meera asks you to write a short update for her boss: the vendor report is two days late because the vendor changed their data format. Write 2–3 sentences she can forward as-is.
scenes.rubric: Clear and polite. States the delay (2 days) and the reason (vendor changed data format) in plain language. Offers a next step or new date. No blame, no jargon, under 80 words.
scenes.placeholder: Hi Arjun, a quick update on the vendor report…

scenes.text: Riya from the next desk is stuck on a spreadsheet and asks for help. You still have your own report to finish before you leave.

choices.text: Help Riya. Your report can wait an hour
choices.outcome: You fix her formula in 20 minutes. She's grateful, but now you're staying late.

choices.text: Politely say you're swamped and point her to a tutorial
choices.outcome: Riya says "no worries" and turns back to her screen. Your report gets done on time.

scenes.text: You finally shut your laptop. The bus ride home is 50 minutes. You're tired, but you made it through day one.

days.title: Tuesday: the big meeting
days.realTalk: PLACEHOLDER: replace with a real quote, e.g. "Meetings are where you find out whether anyone read your email."

scenes.text: Riya drops a cutting chai on your desk. "For yesterday. Also, I heard the client is going to ask about the vendor delay. Thought you'd want a heads-up."
Riya is chatting with the team about the client meeting. You catch the end of it: something about the vendor delay. Nobody fills you in.
In the client call, the client asks sharply why the vendor report is late. Meera glances at you.

choices.text: Explain calmly what happened and give the new date
choices.outcome: The client nods. Meera messages you afterwards: "Well handled."

choices.text: Stay quiet and let Meera answer
choices.outcome: Meera handles it, but you wonder if you missed a chance.

choices.text: Offer to send a detailed written update after the call
choices.outcome: The client agrees. One more thing on your to-do list, but it buys time.

scenes.text: It's the end of a long day. There's a pile of small tasks left. What do you do?

choices.text: Stay an extra hour and clear them all
choices.outcome: Empty to-do list. Tired, but satisfied.

choices.text: Write tomorrow's list and leave on time
choices.outcome: You're home in time for dinner. The tasks will be there tomorrow.
